This '''list of spirals''' includes named [[spirals]] that have been described mathematically.

{| class="wikitable sortable"
! scope="col" | Image
! scope="col" | Name
! scope="col" | First described
! scope="col" | Equation
! scope="col" | Comment
|-
| [[File:Circle - black simple.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Circle]] 
| 
| <math>r= k</math> 
| The trivial spiral
|-
| [[File:Archimedean spiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Archimedean spiral]] (also ''arithmetic spiral'') 
| {{sort|-300|{{circa|320 BC}}}} 
| <math>r=a+b \cdot \theta </math> 
|
|-
| [[File:Fermat's spiral.svg|75px|none]]
| [[Fermat's spiral]] (also parabolic spiral) 
| 1636{{r|Fermat}}
| <math>r^{2} = a^{2} \cdot \theta</math>
| Encloses equal area per turn
|-
| [[File:PSM V79 D459 Logarithmic spiral in flower growth configuration.png|75px|none]]
| [[Doyle spiral]]
| 1980{{mdash}}1990{{r|Doyle}}
| 
| circle packing, using circles of structured radii
|-
| [[File:Cornu Spiral.svg|75px|none]]
| [[Euler spiral]] (also {{em|Cornu spiral}} or polynomial spiral) 
| 1696<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Cornu Spiral |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-11-22 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
| <math>x(t) = \operatorname{C}(t),\,</math><math>y(t) = \operatorname{S}(t)</math>
| Using [[Fresnel integral|Fresnel integrals]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Fresnel Integrals |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-01-31 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
|-
| [[File:Hyperspiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Hyperbolic spiral]] (also ''reciprocal spiral'') 
| 1704 
| <math>r = \frac{a}{\theta}</math>
|
|-
| [[File:Lituus.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Lituus (mathematics)|Lituus]] 
| 1722 
| <math>r^{2} \cdot \theta = k </math>
|
|-
| [[File:Logarithmic Spiral Pylab.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Logarithmic spiral]] (also known as ''equiangular spiral'') 
| 1638{{r|Descartes}} 
| <math>r=a\cdot e^{b \cdot \theta}</math>
| Constant [[Pitch angle (spiral)|pitch angle]]. Approximations of this are found in nature
|-
| [[File:Fibonacci spiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Fibonacci spiral]] 
| 
| [[Circular arc]]s connecting the opposite corners of squares in the Fibonacci tiling 
| Approximation of the golden spiral
|-
| [[File:Golden spiral in rectanglesflip.png|75px|none]] 
| [[Golden spiral]] 
| 
| <math>r = \varphi^{\frac{2 \cdot \theta}{\pi}}\,</math>
| Special case of the logarithmic spiral
|-
| [[File:Spiral of Theodorus.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Spiral of Theodorus]] (also known as ''Pythagorean spiral'') 
| {{sort|-500|{{circa|500 BC}}}}
| Contiguous right triangles composed of one leg with unit length and the other leg being the hypotenuse of the prior triangle
| Approximates the Archimedean spiral 
|-
| [[File:Involute of circle.png|75px|none]] 
| [[Involute]] 
| 1673 
| <math>x(t)=r(\cos(t+a)+t\sin(t+a)),</math>
<math>y(t)=r(\sin(t+a)-t \cos(t+a))</math>
| Involutes of a circle appear like Archimedean spirals
|-
| [[File:Helix.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Helix]] 
| 
| <math>r(t) = 1,\,</math> <math>\theta(t) = t,\,</math> <math>z(t) = t</math>
| A three-dimensional spiral
|-
| [[File:Loxodrome.png|75px|none]] 
| [[Rhumb line]] (also loxodrome) 
| 
| 
| Type of spiral drawn on a sphere
|-
| [[File:Epi half spirals.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Cotes's spiral]] 
| 1722 
| <math>
\frac{1}{r} = 
\begin{cases}
 A \cosh(k\theta + \varepsilon) \\
 A \exp(k\theta + \varepsilon) \\
 A \sinh(k\theta + \varepsilon) \\
 A (k\theta + \varepsilon) \\
 A \cos(k\theta + \varepsilon) \\
\end{cases}
</math>
| Solution to the two-body problem for an inverse-cube central force
|-
| [[File:PoinsotSpiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Poinsot's spirals]] 
| 
| <math> r = a \cdot \operatorname{csch}(n \cdot \theta),\, </math><br/><math> r = a \cdot \operatorname{sech}(n \cdot \theta) </math>
|
|-
| [[File:Nielsen's spiral.png|75px|none]] 
| [[Nielsen's spiral]] 
| 1993{{r|Nelsen}} 
| <math>x(t) = \operatorname{ci}(t),\,</math><br/><math>y(t) = \operatorname{si}(t)</math> 
| A variation of Euler spiral, using [[Trigonometric integral#Sine integral|sine integral]] and cosine integrals
|-
| [[File:Polygon spiral.png|75px|none]] 
| [[Polygonal spiral]]
| 
| 
| Special case approximation of arithmetic or logarithmic spiral
|-
| [[File:Fraser spiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Fraser spiral illusion|Fraser's Spiral]] 
| 1908 
| 
| Optical illusion based on spirals
|-
| [[File:Conchospiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Conchospiral]] 
| 
| <math>r = \mu^{t} \cdot a,\,</math><math>\theta = t,\,</math><math>z = \mu^{t} \cdot c</math>
| A three-dimensional spiral on the surface of a cone.
|-
| [[File:Calkin-Wilf spiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Calkin–Wilf tree|Calkin–Wilf spiral]] 
| 
| 
|
|-
| [[File:Ulam spiral howto primes only.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Ulam spiral]] (also prime spiral) 
| 1963 
| 
|
|-
| [[File:Sacks spiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Ulam spiral#Variants|Sacks spiral]] 
| 1994 
| 
| Variant of Ulam spiral and Archimedean spiral.
|-
|  
| [[Seiffert's spiral]] 
| 2000<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Seiffert's Spherical Spiral |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-01-31 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
| <math>r = \operatorname{sn}(s, k),\,</math><math>\theta = k \cdot s</math><math>z = \operatorname{cn}(s, k)</math>
| Spiral curve on the surface of a sphere using the [[Jacobi elliptic functions]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Seiffert's Spherical Spiral |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-01-31 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
|-
| [[File:Tractrix Spiral.svg |75px|none]] 
| [[Tractrix]] spiral 
| 1704{{r|tractrix}} 
| <math>\begin{cases} r = A \cos(t) \\ \theta = \tan(t ) -t\end{cases}</math>
|
|-
|  
| [[Pappus spiral]]
| 1779 
| <math>\begin{cases} r=a \theta \\ \psi = k \end{cases}</math>
| 3D conical spiral studied by [[Pappus of Alexandria|Pappus]] and [[Blaise Pascal|Pascal]]{{r|Pappus}}
|-
| [[File:Doppler spiral.svg|75px|none]]
| [[Doppler spiral]]
| 
| <math>x = a \cdot ( t \cdot \cos(t) + k \cdot t),\,</math><math>y = a \cdot t \cdot \sin(t)</math>
| 2D projection of Pappus spiral{{r|doppler}}
|-
| [[File:Atzema spiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Atzema spiral]]
| 
| <math>x = \frac{\sin(t)}{t} - 2 \cdot \cos(t) - t \cdot \sin(t),\,</math><math>y = -\frac{\cos(t)}{t} - 2 \cdot \sin(t) + t \cdot \cos(t)</math>
| The curve that has a [[Caustic (mathematics)|catacaustic]] forming a circle. Approximates the Archimedean spiral.{{r|Atzema}}
|-
| [[File:AtomicSpiral.svg|75px|none]] 
| [[Atomic spiral]]
| 2002 
| <math>r = \frac{\theta}{\theta - a}</math>
| This spiral has two [[Asymptote|asymptotes]]; one is the circle of radius 1 and the other is the line <math>\theta=a</math>{{r|atomic}}
|-
| [[File:Galaxy NGC1079.jpg|75px|none]] 
| [[Galactic spiral]]
| 2019 
| <math>\begin{cases} dx=R \cdot \frac{y}{\sqrt{x^2 +y^2}} d\theta  \\ dy=R \cdot \left[\rho(\theta)- \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}} \right] d\theta \end{cases}   
    \begin{cases} x= \sum dx  \\ \\ \\ y= \sum dy + R \end{cases}</math>
| The differential spiral equations were developed to simulate the spiral arms of disc galaxies, have 4 solutions with three different cases:<math>\rho < 1, \rho = 1, \rho >1</math>, the spiral patterns are decided by the behavior of the parameter <math> \rho </math>.  For <math> \rho <1 </math>, spiral-ring pattern; <math>\rho = 1, </math> regular spiral; <math>\rho > 1,</math> loose spiral. R is the distance of spiral starting point (0, R) to the center. The calculated x and y have to be rotated backward by (<math> -\theta </math>) for plotting.{{r|galactic-1}}{{pred |date=July 2024}}
|}
